steps: 1. Identify admin/user role differences in the app

purpose: Use common passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts
steps: 1. Gather list of valid usernames (email harvest, LinkedIn)
2. Compile a list of 5-10 common passwords
3. Use hydra or spray tool to test each password against all users
4. Monitor for rate limiting/lockouts

name: Kerberoasting
purpose: Extract service account hashes from Kerberos tickets
steps: 1. Enumerate domain users and SPNs (BloodHound, ldapdomaindump)

4. Use cracked password for lateral movement

name: NTLM Hash Cracking
purpose: Crack captured NTLM hashes using dictionary or brute force
steps: 1. Capture NTLM hash via Responder or secretsdump

3. Run hashcat: hashcat -m 1000 hash.txt rockyou.txt
4. Try online lookup (crackstation.net)

purpose: Poison LLMNR/NBT-NS name resolution to capture hashes
steps: 1. Identify targets on same subnet listening for names

name: PowerShell Remoting (WinRM)
purpose: Execute commands on remote Windows hosts via WinRM
steps: 1. Identify hosts with WinRM enabled (port 5985/5986)

4. Run credential dumping: Invoke-Mimikatz

purpose: Use stolen SSH credentials or keys to move between hosts
steps: 1. Capture SSH keys from current host (history, configs)
2. Check for passwordless SSH to internal hosts
3. Add key to ssh-agent: ssh-add key
4. Connect to internal hosts

name: Pass-the-Hash
purpose: Authenticate using NTLM hash without knowing the password
steps: 1. Obtain NTLM hash (secretsdump, mimikatz, capture)
2. Use crackmapexec or evil-winrm: -H <hash>
3. Check admin access on target subnets
4. Execute commands via WMI, PsExec, or WinRM

purpose: Execute commands remotely via Windows SMB service
steps: 1. Confirm SMB is open (port 445)

4. Execute commands on remote host

name: WMI Lateral Movement
purpose: Use Windows Management Instrumentation for remote execution
steps: 1. Verify WMI service running on target port 135

name: Sudo/SUID Privilege Escalation
purpose: Exploit misconfigured sudo rules or SUID binaries for root
steps: 1. Run sudo -l to list allowed commands
2. Check for NOPASSWD entries and command wildcards
3. Find SUID binaries: find / -perm -4000
4. Search GTFOBins for exploitation techniques
5. Use perl -c, find -delete, or awk to escalate

name: Kernel Exploit for Privilege Escalation
purpose: Exploit kernel vulnerabilities to escalate privileges
steps: 1. Get kernel version: uname -a
2. Identify architecture and distribution
3. Search for local exploits (exploit-db, google)
4. Upload and compile exploit on target
5. Run exploit to get root shell

name: Docker Escape Privilege Escalation
purpose: Escape Docker containers to gain host access
steps: 1. Check if running in Docker: cat /proc/1/cgroup
2. Look for mounted sockets: ls -la /var/run/docker.sock
3. If docker.sock mounted, run privileged container
4. Mount host filesystem and chroot
5. Or use CVE exploits for specific Docker versions

name: Unquoted Service Path

steps: 1. Enumerate services: sc query

steps: 1. Find Jenkins with /script console accessible

name: Credential Dumping (Mimikatz)
purpose: Extract plaintext passwords, hashes, and Kerberos tickets
steps: 1. Check for admin/SYSTEM privileges
2. Run mimikatz: privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords
3. Dump LSASS memory or use lsadump::sam for SAM
4. Extract credentials from browsers and applications
5. Use credentials for lateral movement

name: Domain Reconnaissance (PowerSploit)
purpose: Enumerate Active Directory domain for attack paths
steps: 1. Import PowerSploit or Invoke-Expression from GitHub
2. Run Get-NetComputer, Get-NetUser, Get-NetGroup
3. Find domain admins and privileged accounts
4. Identify trusts and unconstrained delegation
5. Plan attack path with BloodHound data

name: LSASS Memory Dump
purpose: Dump LSASS process memory to extract credentials
steps: 1. Identify LSASS process PID: Get-Process lsass
2. Use ProcDump or rundll32 comsvcs MiniDump
3. Transfer dump to analysis machine
4. Parse with mimikatz: sekurlsa::minidump lsass.dmp
5. Extract plaintext or Kerberos tickets

name: Registry Persistence
purpose: Create persistent backdoor via Windows registry autorun
steps: 1. Identify startup locations (Run, RunOnce, AppInit_DLLs)
2. Write payload to HKLM or HKCU registry keys
3. Use scheduled task via schtasks
4. Set up WMI event subscription
5. Verify persistence survives reboot

name: Cron-based Persistence
purpose: Use cron jobs as persistence mechanism on Linux systems
steps: 1. Write backdoor to /tmp or other writable location

3. Also use /etc/cron.d/, /etc/cron.daily/ for root cron
4. Use systemd timers as alternative
5. Set up SSH authorized_keys as backup

name: SOCKS Proxy via SSH
purpose: Set up SOCKS proxy through compromised host for internal browsing
steps: 1. Identify a host with SSH access to internal network
2. Set up dynamic port forwarding: ssh -D 1080 user@target
3. Configure browser/proxychains to use localhost:1080
4. Browse internal services through the proxy
5. Chain additional pivots as needed

name: Port Forwarding and Pivoting
purpose: Access internal services by forwarding ports through compromised hosts
steps: 1. Identify internal IP ranges from current host
2. Use SSH -L or -R for local/remote port forwarding
3. Chisel or ligolo for dynamic multi-hop tunnels
4. Route traffic through proxychains
5. Access internal-only services

name: SSHuttle VPN over SSH
purpose: Transparent proxy/VPN over SSH for routing traffic through target networks
steps: 1. Confirm SSH access to a pivot host
2. Run sshuttle: sshuttle -r user@pivot 10.0.0.0/8

4. All traffic to subnet now routes through pivot
5. Use normal tools (nmap, curl) against internal targets

name: Cloud Metadata Service Exploitation
purpose: Exploit exposed cloud metadata endpoints for credential theft
steps: 1. Identify SSRF or shell access on cloud instance
